validations.droid_claim:
[P0] Compilation error: wrong isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() overload

`UsernameForm.authenticate()` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but `UsernamePasswordForm` defines `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` and requires a `UserModel` parameter. This will not compile; pass `context.getUser()` (or add a no-arg overload that delegates) so the call matches the available method signature.
validations.impact: The code will not compile. UsernameForm.authenticate() calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only definition in the parent class UsernamePasswordForm requires a UserModel parameter. This blocks the entire build.
validations.reasoning: UsernameForm extends UsernamePasswordForm. At line 47 of UsernameForm.java, the call is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with zero arguments. The only definition of this method is at line 160 of UsernamePasswordForm.java: `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`, which requires one parameter. There is no no-arg overload anywhere in the class hierarchy (confirmed via grep). All other call sites in UsernamePasswordForm correctly pass `context.getUser()`. This is a straightforward Java compilation error.
